claims.sentence: Recent systems retrieve the cited work, locate candidate evidence and assign a verdict, typically including a partial-support category \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier,sadeghi2026deepsciverify,lee2026reflens,li2026bibagent}.
claims.claim: BibAgent retrieves the cited work, locates candidate evidence and assigns a verdict that includes a partial-support category.
claims.excerpt: The Cited Source Accessibility Classifier (CSAC) then attempts DOI resolution, publisher full-text retrieval, and open-access surrogate matching for each referenced source. ... query an LRM (e.g., gemini-2.5-pro (Google, 2025)) to decide whether the citation is supported, miscitated, or undecidable.
claims.location: Sec. 3.1 Citation Parsing and Accessibility Routing; Sec. 3.2 ACSV Phase IV (pp. 4-5)
claims.note: Retrieval, evidence localization (ACSV) and a verdict are stated, but the verdict is supported / miscitation / undecidable. There is no partial-support category: graded problems are handled as miscitation error codes (e.g., Scope Extrapolation, Evidence Characterization), not as partial support. Suggested rewording: 'Recent systems retrieve the cited work or take it as input, locate candidate evidence and assign a verdict; some add a partial-support category \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier}.' (cite all five for the first clause, only these two for the partial-support clause).

claims.sentence: Retrieval is incomplete: RefVerifier resolved 57.6\% of references in its test manuscripts to full text \citep{mocan2026refverifier}, and BibAgent infers support for paywalled sources from how other papers cite them rather than from the source itself \citep{li2026bibagent}.
claims.claim: BibAgent judges citations to paywalled sources from how downstream papers cite them, not from the source text.
claims.excerpt: ICSV handles citations whose sources are paywalled or otherwise inaccessible. Rather than attempting to reconstruct the missing full text, it treats the research community as a noisy, distributed memory of the source. The key idea is an Evidence Committee: a set of downstream open-access papers that cite the paywalled source B and whose local citation contexts are distilled into aspect-specific evidence statements.
claims.location: Sec. 3.3 ICSV: The Evidence Committee Mechanism (p. 5)
claims.note: Supported. Minor context: ICSV abstains (Undecidable) when there are too few witness papers (K_min = 6).
